children: The Fed needs to take further action to tame elevated inflation--and if price increases remain persistent, rate hikes at back-to-back meetings aren't out of the question, New York Fed President John Williams says. In a speech at University of Mount St. Vincent in the Bronx, Williams says, "we must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis." Speaking to reporters afterwards, he says those actions could include back-to-back rate hikes, which would mark an accelerated pace of tightening after the Fed skipped following September's rate increase with another in October. "I would not exclude ... moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed, if that's what the information was telling us," Williams says. (matt.grossman@wsj.com; @mattgrossman)

title: Fed's Williams Won't Rule Out Consecutive Rate Hikes — Market Talk
